correctness.rationale: Exact squared-distance enumeration gives multiplicities 24,12,24,24,4,3. The 24-edge graph has rank 11; the 14/36/24 face stage is a connected closed surface with cyclic vertex links and Euler characteristic 2. An actual 80-elementary-pair simplicial collapse is exhaustively replayed from all 240 faces, leaving exactly the 80-face four-crosspolytope boundary. The next stage is the join of seven opposite pairs, and the final stage has universal cube-corner vertices. Each stage is thus identified up to integral homotopy, with no degree repeating across boundaries, proving the entire integral barcode. All exact assertions were checked with bundled files `verify.py` and `collapse_8.json`; numerical tests are not substituted for the finite exhaustive certificate.

value.rationale: The full exact integral Vietoris–Rips persistence of the natural fourteen-vertex rhombic dodecahedron fills a specifically motivated Catalan-solid classification gap highlighted in Saleh’s 2023 dissertation (printed p.75). Unlike a selective rank recomputation, it determines all six Euclidean thresholds, a nontrivial simplicial reduction onto a three-sphere, and the successive geometric two-, three-, and six-sphere phases. This is an intrinsic, reusable benchmark for Rips topology of non-vertex-transitive polyhedral point clouds. The claim is a complete classification of one canonical finite object, not an arbitrary sliced invariant; future uses include exact persistence test data and comparisons with radial deformations. Its value is not claimed to be a general theorem for all Catalan solids.
